automatically harvesting semantic relations from large corpora.
the automatic discovery of semantic relations from text.

the development of new techniques for the automatic extraction of semantic relations between entities from text, with the aim to improve the quality of the results and to reduce the effort required to build a system for a new relation.

Espresso outperforms all the other systems in all the datasets and tasks.

our method is the best performing system for extracting semantic relations from text, with a precision of 0.81 and a recall of 0.72 on a general corpus and a precision of 1.00 and a recall of.85 on a domain-specific corpus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Espresso can be used as an off-the-shelf tool for harvesting semantic relations, and can be easily adapted to new domains.

we have developed a novel approach to extract semantic relations from text, which is based on the exploitation of patterns and their reliability, and which is applicable for both general and specific relations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
generic patterns can be effectively used to filter out incorrect instances, thus improving the overall performance of a relation extraction system.
, when combined with a principled measure for pattern and instance reliability, generic patterns can be exploited for harvesting semantic relations in a general and effective way.
generic patterns, when used in a principled manner, provide an important source of information for weakly-supervised relation harvesting systems.
